messages.subject: sleeplog ID handling in ggir2.9-0 vs. 2.8-2 part 4 error and g.logload error
messages.subject_clean: sleeplog ID handling in ggir2.9-0 vs. 2.8-2 part 4 error and g.logload error
messages.body_plain:
Hi team,

I've had some issues in advanced sleep log handling in the new ggir update.

In the old version of ggir (2.8-2), the sleeplog file with character id vbls (e.g., "001") was linking with the GENEactiv id numbers "001" (admitedly, it only worked when sleeplogidnum=TRUE, despite the vbl being a character vbl).

However, on another computer with ggir2.9-0, the sleeplogs are not linking.
I tested the problem with g.logload and am pinning the problem down to the character formatting.

> sleeplog <-  g.loadlog(loglocation="GGIRadvdiaryT1full_TIB_00ch.csv",
+                        meta.sleep.folder= "comparisonoutput/.../meta/ms3.out",
+                        colid=1, coln1=4,
+                        nnights=14,
+                        sleeplogidnum=TRUE )
Error in g.loadlog(loglocation = "GGIRadvdiaryT1full_TIB_00ch.csv", meta.sleep.folder = "comparisonoutput/nd_A5T5_e5/output_t1_bin_files_copy/meta/ms3.out",  :
  unused argument (sleeplogidnum = TRUE)
>

This error makes sense considering a previous post identifying a change in the code (https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/zjMjnHhXWfA/m/xlYk9m-rHgAJ)

> sleeplog <-  g.loadlog(loglocation="GGIRadvdiaryT1full_TIB_00ch.csv",
+                        meta.sleep.folder= "comparisonoutput/.../meta/ms3.out",
+                        colid=1, coln1=4,
+                        nnights=14,
+                        #sleeplogidnum=TRUE
+                        )
Error in sleeplog[cnt, 1] <- as.character(S[j, colid]) :
  replacement has length zero
In addition: Warning message:
None of the IDs in the accelerometer data could be matched with the ID numbers in the sleeplog. You may want to check that the ID format in your sleeplog is consistent with the ID column in the GGIR part2 csv-report, and that argument coldid is correctly set.
>

This error is replicated when diary is in ggir shell. The text file attached has code I have been using.

My first thought was that the character id column of the sleep log was an issue, but I can't create leading zeros in a number column, and editing all actigraph file id numbers is not an option due to the scale of the project.

The ms2 output shows there may be a space at the end of the actigraph bin file id. But this wasn't an issue in the previous version.

Another possibility I checked was that there were no empty ids in the sleep log - there was full data there. But there is one actigraph file with no id listed - i doubt this is the issue, but perhaps.

I would love to hear your thoughts, work arounds, or specification issues for this problem.

Thank you,
Emily

Would it be possible for you to send me a test example of your problem:
One file from the meta/basic folder

You can send this via personal e-mail if you are worried about sharing data in this google group.

Thanks, Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Time not correct in summary files
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Time not correct in summary files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rob,

Thanks for reaching out to the list and for providing an example file. I processed your file with:

GGIR(
  datadir = "..../RobPryce2306/data",
  outputdir = "..../RobPryce2306",
  desiredtz = "America/Belize",
  configtz = "America/Belize",
  mode = 1:2,
  do.report = 2,
  overwrite = TRUE)

The start time in both daysummary.csv and in summary.csv is 7:30 as you expect.
I am not able to reproduce your part2_daysummary_longformat.csv file because there is only 5 hours of data in your test file. So, I tested this in another file from a different project and used qwindow = c(0, 4, 8, 12, 18, 22, 24) and this indicated that start time was correct:  The first timewindow in daysummary_longformat overlaps with the starttime in part2_summary.csv (which is the same in part2_daysummary.csv).

Could the issue be that you are specifying the timezone as "CST" and not as a timezone database name as I do above? A typical timezone database name involves a continent followed by a forward slash followed by a city: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones.

Thanks,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

------- Original Message -------

On Wednesday, May 31st, 2023 at 3:52 PM, Rob Pryce <rober...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi everyone,
>
> Thanks for creating such a great resource!
>
> I'm working on some day-segment analysis with .gt3x files and am finding the times are offset in the output, but not in the raw data or meta files:
>
> The data was initialized/collected and analyzed in CST (Canada), however the output in the summary files appears to be offset by +11 hours. In this case, the recording should run 0730-1300, but instead the output has times starting at 1830 and running into the next day (i.e. apparent when running 1-hr windows via qwindow). This also means the times in any activity log do not align (unless they are also offset by the 11 hours).
>
> The timestamps in the meta files appear to be correct, as well as in basic plots of epoched enmo in the meta files and the raw gt3x read into R (read.gt3x).
>
> I've tried various changes to desiredtz and configtz, but they most often have no effect.
>
> I'm using Rstudio (R 4.1.0) on Windows 10. Attached is a sample meta file and long format summary file with the offset (generated from 1-hr windows via qwindow). Here's a sample GT3X file: https://www.dropbox.com/s/6mw0idwwigtckq0/sample.gt3x?dl=0
>
> Any suggestions?
>
> Thanks in advance,
> Rob
>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

Thanks so much for the reply.

I processed the sample file using the above and can confirm the same - the start time in the summary csv is correct. (and yes, we'd been using that timezone db name format: continent/city).

However, the offset arises when adding qwindow to isolate a specific time segment (i.e. as in the 'day segment analysis' vignette). In that case, a long format day summary file gets generated, but with that +11 hour offset:

GGIR(
  datadir = i,
  outputdir = o,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  sensor.location = 'hip',

  mode = 1:2,
  do.report = 2,
  desiredtz = "America/Belize",
  configtz = "America/Belize",

  do.enmo = TRUE,
  includedaycrit = 0.1,
  qwindow = c(0, 4, 8, 12, 18, 22, 24))

The files are partial day recordings (5hrs) & I'm interested in the activity occurring ~08:00-10:00.

Attached are the summary files, where 'Part2_summary' has the correct start time, but both daysummary files appear to have that +11hr time offset in the various fields (e.g., weekday, M5hr, qwindow_timestamps, etc).

Any suggestions? As you mention, is it that a full 24 hour recording is required for qwindow, etc? or something else I'm missing?

Thanks again,
Rob

On Friday, May 26, 2023 at 8:23:20 AM UTC-6 Laura Grau wrote:
> Thank you! I will e-mail you an example file.
>
> This is the code I used:
>
> GGIR(datadir = "Baseline", # folder with epoch level .CSV
>      outputdir = "ActiWatchProcessed",
>      dataFormat = "actiwatch_csv",
>      mode = 1:5,
>      do.report = c(2, 4, 5),
>      windowsizes = c(30, 900, 3600), # 15 is the expected epoch length but my length is 30 seconds
>      visualreport = FALSE,
>      outliers.only = FALSE,
>      HASIB.algo = "Sadeh1994",
>      def.noc.sleep = c())
>
> I got these errors:
>
> Error in if (epSizeShort != params_general[["windowsizes"]][1]) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed In addition: Warning messages: 1: When dataFormat is set to actiwatch_csv we assume that metric is ZCY, this is now used 2: When dataFormat is set to actiwatch_csv we assume that only metric ZCY is extracted and GGIR ignores all other metric requests. So, you should set arguments do.anglez & do.enmo to FALSE 3: Be aware that you are using epoch level aggregates of raw data computed outside GGIR by which their reproducibility and transparancy is also outside the scope of GGIR. GGIR input arguments related to raw data handling are ignored.

> >
> > It is intended to work with Actiwath .csv and .AWD files.
> >
> > Here you can see some documentation for how to use it:
> > https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/man/GGIR.Rd#L1384-L1408

> >
> > To install this version of GGIR do:
> >
> > install.packages("remotes')
> > remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "2.9-2")
> >
> > If you have problems please report back and sent me an example file to look at.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

Thanks for the quick reply and assistance.

That's the same output I have, so perhaps the error is on my end in interpretation?

For example, when looking at the rows for each qwindow_timestamp, do the 'N_valid_hours' columns (E, G) not indicate activity occurred at 18:00-22:00 & 22:00-24:00? Likewise, the other ENMO outputs fall in those bins (and M5 appears to start at 1900).

However, the data collection occurred 0730-1300 & accelerometers did not collect past 1300, so I'm not sure why the PA outcomes are showing up in windows later in the day versus 08:00-12:00, etc.

Thank you again for your time - if this falls outside of the assistance/queries on this list please let me know.

see you,
Rob

>
>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Laura,

I have now tested it, and it seems that the main problem is that the code currently only considers date format d-m-Y and if that fails tries again with d/m/Y, e.g. 14-8-2018. I know this is not flexible enough as you have format m/d/y, e.g. 8/14/18.

I have opened an issue for it: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues/798/ to remind us to address this.

It should not be a lot of work, but I need to figure out when I or Jairo have time as the upcoming weeks/month already look packed with other work.

At least for now, it is good to have this as a clear action point and to have a test file.

Thanks,

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Rob,

You are running an analysis to find the most active 5 hours on a 5 hours file. Most of GGIR's functionality is designed for recordings that last at least one day. For recordings shorter than 1 day I think it is best not rely too heavily on circadian rhythm and sleep estimates.

If you can replicate the non-intuitive result in a recording that lasts at least one day then I am happy to have another look.

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Wei,

To follow-up on my previous message, it may be good to elaborate a bit more on the reason why this was a bug:

GGIR originally sorted the full path to the filenames and the filenames only before processing them. This is no problem when all files are in the same folder, but becomes a problem when working with folder names that influence the ordering.

Example 1:

folderA/file1
folderA/file2
folderB/file3
folderB/file4
This will order to: file1, file2, file3, file 4. All is good because that is also what we get when we simply order the filenames without path.

Example 2:

folderA/file3
folderA/file4
folderB/file1
folderB/file2
This will reorder to file3, file4, file1, file 2. This is not good, because filename ordering is different from full path ordering.

To address this I removed all ordering of filenames in GGIR and left the ordering all the way to the end just at the report creation step.

Best,

Vincent

------- Original Message -------

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR 2.9.0 ID errors
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] GGIR 2.9.0 ID errors
messages.body_plain:
Dear Wei,

> I do not know how to manipulate the bin file and I do not think I can do it.

It is not the file itself but the name of the file. Someone changed the number zero to a letter O in the filename. I know this because the GENEActiv software always stores the ID as entered in both the filename and the fileheader.

When setting argument idloc=1, GGIR tries to use the ID from the file header, while when idloc=2 (or any other number) GGIR aims to extract the ID from the filename. This has been the case for a long time, even long before the 2.2-0 release in 2020. In the script "BATS_ggir0.callpipeline.R" you sent me you have argument idloc = 1, which indicates that you were telling GGIR to extract the ID from the file header.

If this worked in the past, then the fact that it worked was a bug, because it should not have worked when ID log in the file header is not consistent with the ID in the sleeplog. Possibly the bug was the subfolder bug I mentioned before that linked the wrong ID to the wrong filename.

An alternative explanation is that you used idloc = 2 in the past and changed it to 1, but I trust that you would be aware of such change.

A third explanation is that someone change the ID in the sleep diary not realising that it is not the ID in the accelerometer file name that is used when idloc = 1 but the ID in the file header.

Either way, the solution is to not set idloc = 1 when you do not trust the ID in the file header. I just tested this with idloc=2 on your file and it works: GGIR produces the attached part 4 reports.

Best,

Vincent

>

> An alternative explanation is that you used idloc = 2 in the past and changed it to 1, but I trust that you would be aware of such change.
>
> A third explanation is that someone change the ID in the sleep diary not realising that it is not the ID in the accelerometer file name that is used when idloc = 1 but the ID in the file header.
>
> Either way, the solution is to not set idloc = 1 when you do not trust the ID in the file header. I just tested this with idloc=2 on your file and it works: GGIR produces the attached part 4 reports.

messages.subject: Rationale sleep efficiency calculation pt4?
messages.subject_clean: Rationale sleep efficiency calculation pt4?
messages.body_plain:
Hey everyone!

When looking into the results of part4, I noticed that "Sleep efficiency" (the non-default variable, only available when a sleeplog is used) is calculated as: SleepDurationInSpt / guider_inbedDuration. I was wondering why "guider_inbedDuration" was used as denominator and not "SptDuration + sleep latency"? In other words, why participant-indicated-wake-up-time is used in stead of the algorithm-identified-wake-up-time to indicate the ending of time in bed?

I'm asking that as for some nights the error_wake (difference between participant-indicated-wake-up-time and algorithm-identified-wake-up-time) is around 2 hours. In the current version of sleep efficiency calculation this results in a very low score as those two hours now count as non-sleep. You could argue that these 2 hours are the time attempting to sleep after final awakening (TASAFA). However, guider_inbedEnd (participant-indicated-wake-up-time) does not represent that attempt, as only final wake up time was asked.

As you can see in the specific example below, wake up was identified by the algorithm at 2:38:10 while the participant reported final awakening at 5:00:00 (out of bed was at 7:15:00 according to the participant, but this is not taking into account in the sleeplog for GGIR). In this specific case, it seems that the algorithm could be off by a few hours. Making the sleep efficiency score less reliable.

Overall, I tend to trust the sleep efficiency score calculated with "SptDuration + sleep latency" more as this uses the algorithm to identify sleep onset, sleep duration, WASO, wake up and only uses the subjective input from the participant to calculate sleep latency. I was wondering what you think as a community and what the rationale was for making guider_inbedDuration as default denominator?

Thanks in advance!
Pieter-Jan Marent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Capability to run GGIR without reaching out to CRAN?
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Capability to run GGIR without reaching out to CRAN?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Diana,

The function zzz inside GGIR uses the base R function package_version to reach out to CRAN to check whether the installed GGIR version is behind the available version on CRAN. If it is, then a message is printed to the console to inform the user about this. GGIR will never install updates itself, all it does is provide a warning.

In my experience GGIR can be used on computing clusters that have no access to the internet. The attempt by package_version to check the package version did not stop me from using the package. However, I appreciate that your cluster may have different requirements or be configured differently.

The solution I would then recommend is to make a fork of https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR, remove the zzz.R function-file from the GGIR/R folder in the branch, and install this branch on your cluster via R library remotes or devtools.

Another approach might be to look for ways to block internet access by GGIR at R or OS level. However, I have no experience with that and you may find better help for that elsewhere.

Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I now realise that the below discussion from April 2023 relates also to the recent work on VILPA (Vigorous intermittent, lifestyle physical activity) by Stamatakis and colleagues: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9800274/.

As people are asking me how to extract VILPA with GGIR, I have now tried to better understand what Stamatakis and colleagues did. No open-source licensed code has been shared in the paper that could clarify the calculation of VILPA, which is problematic as the paper comes with major claims about health benefits in a reputable journal without a clear definition of what is being measured! The promise that code will be send to UK Biobank does not make this paper reproducible as we need a direct link to the code for that.

Based on what I understand from the text, VILPA can only be calculated if participants report to never participate in planned exercises such as sport. In the absence of this self-reported information VILPA is reduced to just short lasting VPA that may or may not be part of scheduled exercise. It is less clear whether VPA that is part of an MVPA bouts is counted towards VPA or towards MVPA. The lack of reference to MVPA bouts in the paper gives the impression that MVPA bouts are not considered, by which time spent in VPA effectively reflects some of the time that we previously considered part of MVPA bouts. This would then also explain the strong association with health. The minimum length of 10 seconds is a result of the underlying method and does not seem to be motivated as an essential minimum length of VPA. In other words, using 5 second epochs would also seem justifiable.

As a result, VILPA may then be derived with GGIR in two possible ways depending on how you defined VILPA:
If we want to ignore short lasting VPA that is part of MVPA bouts then set the minimum bout length for MVPA at 1 or 2 minutes and look at unbouted VPA (GGIR part5 output variable "dur_day_VIG_unbt_min").
If we do NOT want to ignore short lasting VPA that is part of MVPA bouts then set the moderate threshold to a value that corresponds with vigorous and tell GGIR to extract 'MVPA' bouts lasting at least 1 or 2 minutes, which then will represent long VPA bouts (named MVPA in the variable name), and your unbouted VPA reflects short lasting VPA bouts regardless of being part in MVPA.

Note that GGIR has facilitated this for a long time, so from a methodological perspective there is nothing new here.

Best wishes,

Vincent

Hello GGIR Community,

When piloting the code on two .cwa files, using only parts 1 and 2, I came across the following error:

 _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Part 2

Busy processing ... see /Users/UKBiobank/Results/output_UKBio_Shared/meta/ms2.out for progress

Error in as.character(Value) :

Dominika

messages.body_plain:
> Another quick question, if GGIR will use inside ID to link the intermediate output if I specify idloc=1 and no sleeplog was used at all.

Intermediate output is linked based on full filename and not based on the ID inside the file, so that should go correct.

Best, Vincent

------- Original Message -------

On Monday, June 5th, 2023 at 11:02 PM, Wei Guo <guowe...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Vincent,
>
> Thank you so much for the detailed illustration. I will re-run the data using idloc=2 instead of idloc=1 for that data. Hope everything runs smoothly.
>
> Another quick question, if GGIR will use inside ID to link the intermediate output if I specify idloc=1 and no sleeplog was used at all.
>
> Thank you so much. Have a great day.
> Best,
> Wei
>
> On Mon, Jun 5, 2023 at 3:54 AM Vincent van Hees <v.va...@accelting.com> wrote:
> > Dear Wei,
> >
> > > I do not know how to manipulate the bin file and I do not think I can do it.
> >
> > It is not the file itself but the name of the file. Someone changed the number zero to a letter O in the filename. I know this because the GENEActiv software always stores the ID as entered in both the filename and the fileheader.
> >
> > When setting argument idloc=1, GGIR tries to use the ID from the file header, while when idloc=2 (or any other number) GGIR aims to extract the ID from the filename. This has been the case for a long time, even long before the 2.2-0 release in 2020. In the script "BATS_ggir0.callpipeline.R" you sent me you have argument idloc = 1, which indicates that you were telling GGIR to extract the ID from the file header.
> >
> > If this worked in the past, then the fact that it worked was a bug, because it should not have worked when ID log in the file header is not consistent with the ID in the sleeplog. Possibly the bug was the subfolder bug I mentioned before that linked the wrong ID to the wrong filename.
> >
> > An alternative explanation is that you used idloc = 2 in the past and changed it to 1, but I trust that you would be aware of such change.
> >
> > A third explanation is that someone change the ID in the sleep diary not realising that it is not the ID in the accelerometer file name that is used when idloc = 1 but the ID in the file header.
> >
> > Either way, the solution is to not set idloc = 1 when you do not trust the ID in the file header. I just tested this with idloc=2 on your file and it works: GGIR produces the attached part 4 reports.
> >
> > Best,
> >
> > Vincent
> >
> > ------- Original Message -------
> > On Monday, June 5th, 2023 at 2:31 AM, Wei Guo <guowe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > > Hi Vincent

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Advanced Sleep Log - (Non-Wear Detection and Nap Time) Quick Question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,

Regarding nonwear detection:
If you use nonwear_approach = "2023" the nonwear detection should be more intuitive. Note that this is not the default yet. Our aim is to make it the default in the 3.0 release as this would affect consistency with old GGIR releases.

Regarding visualisation of self-report nonwear and nap time:
I am expecting to have a new project this summer that will pay for my time to incorporate this as an enhancement to the visualreport. Note that at the moment the self-reported nonwear and napping are not used in GGIR, all it does is archive them but the plan is to integrate them more effectively in GGIR.

Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

Did you check argument minimum_MM_length.part5?

Vincent

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Re: Error with initializing devices ahead of time
messages.body_plain:
Hi Susanna,

It sounds like the device collected a few data points a week prior to the recording then was asleep for a week and then started collected data, where ActiGraph imputed those data points with zeros.

For the time being could you try setting GGIR argument 'minloadcrit = 240'
this will tell GGIR to not attempt the auto-calibration before it has either reached the end of the file or has read at least 10 days of data.

If that does not work, could you sent me an example .gt3x file?

Thanks,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error when using advanced sleeplog (Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2))
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Error when using advanced sleeplog (Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2))
messages.body_plain:
Dear Mikael,

The error indicates that something goes wrong with reading or processing the sleeplog file. Common problems are that ID's do not match or the separator is not valid.

Did you check that ID is correctly extract from the accelerometer file? This can be checked by inspecting the part2_summary.csv report. The ID column in that file should be identical to the ID column in the sleeplog file.

You can check the separator in Notepad for example.

After you change the sleeplog to advanced did you re-run GGIR part 3 and 4?

> I can also share the script and the log if it would help, I could not attach any files to this message.

Yes, that could help, even if it is just the relevant lines.

Thanks,
Vincent

On Thursday, June 8th, 2023 at 3:44 AM, Pieter-Jan Marent <marentp...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hey everyone!
>
> When looking into the results of part4, I noticed that "Sleep efficiency" (the non-default variable, only available when a sleeplog is used) is calculated as: SleepDurationInSpt / guider_inbedDuration. I was wondering why "guider_inbedDuration" was used as denominator and not "SptDuration + sleep latency"? In other words, why participant-indicated-wake-up-time is used in stead of the algorithm-identified-wake-up-time to indicate the ending of time in bed?
>
> I'm asking that as for some nights the error_wake (difference between participant-indicated-wake-up-time and algorithm-identified-wake-up-time) is around 2 hours. In the current version of sleep efficiency calculation this results in a very low score as those two hours now count as non-sleep. You could argue that these 2 hours are the time attempting to sleep after final awakening (TASAFA). However, guider_inbedEnd (participant-indicated-wake-up-time) does not represent that attempt, as only final wake up time was asked.
>
> As you can see in the specific example below, wake up was identified by the algorithm at 2:38:10 while the participant reported final awakening at 5:00:00 (out of bed was at 7:15:00 according to the participant, but this is not taking into account in the sleeplog for GGIR). In this specific case, it seems that the algorithm could be off by a few hours. Making the sleep efficiency score less reliable.
>
> Overall, I tend to trust the sleep efficiency score calculated with "SptDuration + sleep latency" more as this uses the algorithm to identify sleep onset, sleep duration, WASO, wake up and only uses the subjective input from the participant to calculate sleep latency. I was wondering what you think as a community and what the rationale was for making guider_inbedDuration as default denominator?
>
> Thanks in advance!
> Pieter-Jan Marent
>
>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Allison,

I am not able to reproduce your error with GGIR 2.9-4 in Ubuntu.

The only change I made to your code was to ignore the line:

> f1 = as.numeric(length(list.files(shell.input)));f1

because just setting f0 = 1 and f1 = NULL will achieve the same and will adapt to the number of files you provide.

Further, note that the following arguments you specified are not used by GGIR any longer as they have been deprecated: L5M5window and bout.metric.

Did you try running the code in a new output folder or using overwrite = TRUE and deleting the config.csv file generated by GGIR?

If all that does not address the issue, are you sure this example file produces the error?

Thanks,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error when using advanced sleeplog (Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2))
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Error when using advanced sleeplog (Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2))
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mikael,

This is bug in GGIR: There are no sustained inactivity bouts in the first night and GGIR cannot handle this. It is very unusual to not have any of them as it would mean that the person has not rested or slept for the first 24 hours or the device was in ActiGraph idle sleep mode for the first 24 hours, which would explain that I had not seen this before.

I have prepared a fix, which you can try out via installing GGIR as follows:

install.package("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue812_absence_sib_firstday")
library(GGIR)

A second problem is that you did not specify argument idloc when you processed the file with GGIR part 1, by which GGIR did not attempt to extract the ID from the accelerometer file name and as a result will struggle to match this with the ID as stored in the sleeplog.

Kind regards,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.body_plain:
Dear Gareth,

It might be that you have reprocessed those 20 files (as indicated by f1 in your script and overwrite = TRUE) with a different configuration than the rest of the files. Probably you changed any argument that provided a different number of columns in the reports for these 20 files and then the report generation gets this problem.

Is it possible for you to re-run parts 2 to 5 in all your files? Make sure you set f1 to NULL (this would make GGIR using all the files in your datadir), mode = 2:5, and overwrite = TRUE.

Let me know if that solves your issue.

Best,
Jairo
